prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system spans River Intake Pump Station–High Service Pump Header; excludes distribution. Aliases: Ironwood=River Intake Pump Station; Marigold=Coagulant Dosing Skid; Cobalt=North Filter Gallery; Sparrow=Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench; Lantern=SCADA Historian Server; Quarry=Maintenance Planner. Items: Raw Water Screen Channel sends Rake Torque Snapshot; Quarry compares loading. Marigold sends Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies identity, sends Sample Chain Slip. Sparrow receives custody-controlled samples, sends checked Jar Test Photograph Set. South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note. Chemical Supplier Driver sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading; Residuals Hauler removes residuals. Distribution Dispatcher receives demand/production/header notices.
Intake obeys withdrawal/demand/depth/permissives; losses alarm/stop. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode; intensify sampling until raw/settled stability; re-review discretionary work. Duty Engineer approves temporary changes/reconciles results. Dosing-feedback loss requires verified safe dosing/grabs. Filters monitor turbidity/headloss; backwash return requires rinse-to-waste stability. Overrides require justification/monitoring/restoration. Samples require custody/acceptance/analytical checks; late/warm samples troubleshooting-only; field results provisional pending reconciliation. Sample Backwash Recovery Tank after consequential returns.
Maintenance requires approved windows, capacity, isolation verification/acknowledgment, shift communication, closure evidence; chemical work requires ventilation/monitoring/communications. Technician confirms sampling/acceptance concerns; Sparrow remains available. Return requires inspection/test/instrument/sample/operator evidence and removal or formal acceptance of temporary equipment/barriers. Failed tests leave orders open; Chief Operator decides isolation/restriction. Lantern retains synchronized results and pre/post-work data; disinfection resumes only after Chief Operator confirms consistent feed/residual/level responses.
Chlorine Contact Basin maintains required contact time versus production/level/residual; adjust feed gradually. Chlorine Residual Alarm pauses maintenance pending cause confirmation; verify analyzer flow/grab comparison, hold production increases; Technician confirms suspected drift/fouling/trends. Clearwell Level Controller protects contact/reserves/pump suction; low-level interlocks prevent unsafe drawdown; high-level alarms prompt production/pumping adjustment.

Document units:
S134: The Clearwell Level Controller sends the Clearwell Diver Entry Permit when level and isolation prerequisites have been verified by the control system.
S135: Clearwell level changes are trended against filter production and high-service demand so that slow instrumentation errors can be distinguished from actual storage changes.
S136: The High Service Pump Header is identified in voice radio traffic by the alias Juniper when operators need a short confirmation name.
S137: The High Service Pump Header sequences available pumps to meet distribution demand while avoiding unnecessary starts, short cycling, and operation near unstable portions of the pump curves.
S138: Lead and lag pump assignments are rotated according to runtime, availability, and any operating restriction entered by the Chief Operator.
S139: Header pressure control uses a paced response so that pump starts, pump speed changes, and valve movements do not create avoidable pressure transients in the distribution system.
S140: The High Service Pump Header produces the Pump Bearing Vibration Clip after a configured vibration threshold is exceeded during pump operation.
S141: If a high-service pump trips, the remaining available pumps are evaluated automatically against the current pressure setpoint before another unit is started.
S142: The North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station receive pressure support through coordinated setpoints that reflect system demand and storage conditions.
S143: The Distribution Dispatcher is identified by the alias Falcon during pressure coordination calls with plant staff.
S144: The Distribution Dispatcher communicates expected demand changes, main break impacts, and pressure complaints so that plant pumping decisions match field conditions.
S145: During Storm Intake Mode, operators watch the relationship between raw water quality, filter loading, disinfectant demand, and high-service pumping to avoid forcing production beyond treatment capability.
S146: Abnormal clearwell level, loss of residual, loss of pump header pressure, or conflicting instrument readings require the Duty Engineer to review the operating condition before setpoints are changed outside normal ranges.
S147: The SCADA Historian Server stores residual, level, pressure, and pump status data at sufficient resolution to support event reconstruction after alarms or customer pressure complaints.
S148: Manual operation is allowed only when the operator can maintain residual targets, clearwell limits, and distribution pressure with direct observation of the affected indications.
S149: Return to automatic control requires stable chlorine residual, stable clearwell level response, and confirmed high-service pressure control for a period set by the Chief Operator.
